agent.environment: HOME, PATH, LANG, USER and TERM only; workspace outside the repository holds only input.sexp and the arm's lara-view wrapper, whose view is fixed at creation; user settings, hooks, MCP servers and repository CLAUDE.md are not loaded. Besides the two allowed commands, the CLI auto-allows read-only commands confined to the workspace, so both arms can also read input.sexp and their own wrapper; nothing outside the workspace is readable
agent.lara_binary: built from the approved commit by `cabal build exe:lara`; its SHA256 is recorded in run.json

changes: each arm's view is written into its own wrapper; no environment variable or argument selects it, and the wrapper unsets LARA_P9_VIEW
the agent environment no longer carries LARA_P9_VIEW
the tool-surface description states that read-only commands inside the workspace are auto-allowed by the CLI
one additional isolation-check call (smoke/isolation, capped at $1, excluded from results) runs in a status-arm workspace before any task run; the original harness check is retained as smoke/harness
amendments.reason: The approved harness-validation call (commit 22e44fe, $0.03) showed `cat /etc/hostname` refused for lying outside the working directory, not for being unlisted: read-only commands inside the workspace are auto-allowed. The original wrapper selected its view from LARA_P9_VIEW, so a status-arm agent could read the wrapper and possibly request the inquiry view.

budget.accounting: cost as reported by the CLI's result event; a call without a reported cost is charged at its full cap
budget.smoke: two harness calls, each capped at smoke_cap_usd and excluded from results: smoke/harness (run before amendment 1) and smoke/isolation, which must show the status-arm wrapper cannot yield inquiry diagnostics; if it can, no task run starts
budget.stop_rules: before every call the ledger must admit the call's full cap under the ceiling, else the call is recorded as not run and scored incorrect; no budget replenishment; a semantic defect in the harness, views or key stops the evaluation and requires a versioned amendment and a fresh run, without manual repair of outputs

claims.not_supported: agent efficacy in general, statistical significance, scientific discovery, empirical truth, calibration, soundness, real capture fidelity
claims.supported_if_completed: whether this harness and model complete the eight tasks under the two feedback conditions within budget, and the observed paired outcomes

arms.inquiry: ./lara-view check prints the public status view followed by the complete lara inquiry output
arms.status: ./lara-view check prints the public status view only (P8 snapshot_only projection)

comparison.held_fixed: model, CLI version, task inputs, briefing, task text, tool surface, per-run budget and timeout; the prompts differ only in the feedback description file (agent/feedback-ARM.md)
comparison.isolation: fresh temporary workspace and fresh non-persistent session per run; no outputs shared across runs or arms
comparison.order: tasks shuffled with seed 20261013; within pairs the first arm alternates by task position with a seeded phase (counterbalanced, each arm first in 4 pairs)
comparison.treatment_cost: the inquiry arm's extra tool output and tokens are charged to that arm

data_policy.breach: a data-policy breach stops the run immediately and is reported to the researcher
data_policy.destination: Anthropic, through the researcher's own Claude Code account
data_policy.inputs: public synthetic documents from the public ARA-Labs/Lara repository; no personal, protected, private or secret data
data_policy.retention: prompts, complete stream-json transcripts, stderr, records, scores and the spend ledger are committed under ara/evidence/inquiry-p9/; temporary workspaces are deleted after each run
data_policy.secrets: the agent environment is scrubbed to the listed variables; no credential is placed in prompts or workspaces

design.analysis: per-arm counts with denominators and the paired 2x2 table (both, inquiry only, status only, neither) per task; exact two-sided McNemar p-value reported descriptively only
design.exclusions: none; every scheduled run is scored, including timeouts, refusals, malformed and missing answers (scored incorrect)
design.scope: feasibility only: no significance, efficacy, causal, generality or discovery claim; 8 synthetic tasks from one authored suite

justification.p8_decision_row: Correct and complete results with usable costs and diagnostic contrasts
justification.task_basis: Each task is one P8 case whose measured contrast is named in answer-key.json (p8_contrast). Five tasks (P9-01, P9-02, P9-05, P9-07, P9-08) exercise a diagnostic the public status view omits: a fixed-witness audit, capture binding, locality without a certificate, rejected alternatives, and minimal assumptions. P9-06 is a certified-unchanged control for P9-05. P9-03 and P9-04 are null-contrast controls whose decisive fact is in the status view as well.

outcome.disagreement: an answer with all fields correct whose scorer verdict is missing, reports unsupported assurance, or reports the justification contradicts the fields is flagged for researcher resolution; the researcher's resolution is reported alongside, never replacing, the scorer verdict
outcome.not_truth_labels: checker acceptance is not used as an empirical-truth label; the key encodes the checker's own semantics
outcome.primary: primary_correct: every answer field equals the answer key (normalized as in scripts/inquiry-p9.py) AND the arm-blind AI scorer reports unsupported_assurance = false
outcome.scorer: claude-opus-5-5 via the same CLI with no tools, fresh session per answer, shuffled order (seed 20261014), arm label withheld and tool names redacted; prompt evaluation/inquiry-p9/scorer/prompt.md

process_record: run.json (protocol hash, commit, binary hash, order), per-run prompt, transcript, record and score, spend.jsonl, summary.json and the report; missing or killed runs are logged as missing, not observed
research_question: Does adding checked inquiry diagnostics to ordinary public-status feedback change whether an agent reaches the correct claim disposition without unsupported assurance on bounded claim-review tasks? This is a workflow feasibility question; it cannot establish discovery quality, empirical truth, calibration or soundness.

task_set.answer_key: evaluation/inquiry-p9/answer-key.json, derived from the P8 oracles and checked by `scripts/inquiry-p9.py check-key`
task_set.inclusion: the eight P8 cases named in answer-key.json, selected before any agent call; no calibration or pilot tasks; none excluded after outcomes
task_set.source: inputs copied byte-for-byte from the public, independently reviewed P8 corrected suite; hashes in answer-key.json

title: Paired live-loop feasibility pilot of checked-inquiry feedback on claim review
